newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 7.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 7.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name products and Consumer Trends.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - France's five billboard advertising firms, Avenir, Dauphin, Giraudy, Marignan and More O'Ferall, seeking to reassure advertisers, have decided to finance surveillance of fly-posting over billboards during the election campaign. They will systematically photograph billboards marred by election posters or graffitti. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - Advertising agency McCann Erikson France says it won the advertising budget for packager Tetra Pak following a competition which in which rival agencies FCB and Grey were also candidates. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - French digital satellite television service Television par Satellite (TPS) say it has now signed 140,000 subscriber contracts. It presents two interactive services, weather forecast service Meteo Express, operational since April 29, and a programme guide, due to come on stream on May 13. (La Tribune)
PARIS - A nude photo of comic actress Valerie Lemercier helped sales of new French women's magazine DS. It sold 180,000 copies out of a print-run of 199,228. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - President Jacques Chirac angers many French newspapers by singling out the 14 biggest provincial dailies to publish his appeal for support in the upcoming election, but most national dailies manage to publish his text anyway. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

ZURICH - Helmut Maucher, chairman and chief executive of Nestle SA, says the company has no intention of selling its stake in French cosmetics company l'Oreal, or of selling its Alcon pharmaceuticals division. (Reuter)
PARIS - Shares in French tobacco company Seita rise after a Florida jury ruled that RJ Reynolds Tobacco was not negligent in a closely-watched wrongful death lawsuit. (Reuter)
CONSUMER TRENDS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Sales made by French hypermarkets rose 1.9 percent in value terms in April, and those made by supermarkets were 2.4 percent higher than in April 1996, retailers' group Federation des Entreprises du Commerce et de la Distribution (FCD) says. (Reuter)

PARIS - A study by ad agency J. Walter Thompson shows French young people aged 20-30 reject stereotypes, talking "cool" and hard-sell advertising. They generally have small incomes but collectively get a global 100 billion francs from parents or grandparents, enough to attract advertisers. (Le Figaro)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
